US Dollar Index Rises After Hot PPI Boosts Fed Rate Hike Bets

Written By: Lilly Mwogah
·
Indices
·1 day ago·
Last updated:1 day ago
Share
Prefer us on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread

The US Dollar Index strengthened on Thursday after hotter-than-expected US producer inflation increased expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at next week’s policy meeting.

The Producer Price Index (PPI) for final demand increased 0.4% month over month in August and 5.4% from a year earlier, according to the latest data. Annual producer inflation came in slightly above the 5.3% economists had expected and accelerated from 4.7% in July.

The data added another layer to the increasingly hawkish Fed outlook following last week’s stronger-than-expected US jobs report. With inflation remaining elevated and oil prices adding to price pressures, investors are increasingly questioning whether the Federal Reserve can keep interest rates unchanged in September.

US PPI Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected

The August US PPI report showed that inflation pressures at the producer level remain persistent. Producer prices increased 0.4% from July, while annual PPI accelerated to 5.4%. Energy prices were a major contributor, jumping 4.2% during the month as the Middle East conflict drove oil prices sharply higher. Food prices increased a more modest 0.1%.

The latest reading follows a comparatively soft July, when the headline PPI was unchanged month over month and increased 4.7% annually. That acceleration matters because producer prices can eventually filter through to consumer inflation, particularly if companies pass higher input costs on to customers.

For the US dollar, persistent inflation strengthens the case for keeping US interest rates higher and potentially raising them again.

US Dollar Gains as Fed Rate Hike Odds Jump

The inflation report prompted another repricing of Federal Reserve interest rate expectations. Traders increased the probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate hike in September to around 70%, from roughly 62% before the PPI report, according to Reuters.

That shift is supportive for the US dollar because higher interest rates can increase the relative attractiveness of dollar-denominated assets.

Treasury yields also moved sharply higher following the inflation data, with the benchmark 10-year yield approaching 4.92%, its highest level since 2023.

The move highlights how quickly the US interest-rate narrative has changed. Markets are no longer primarily debating when the Fed might cut rates; the immediate question is increasingly whether policymakers will need to tighten policy again.

Strong US Jobs Report Adds to Dollar Support

Thursday’s inflation figures follow a much stronger-than-expected August US jobs report, giving policymakers another reason to remain cautious about inflation. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, far exceeding the 56,000 jobs economists had expected, while unemployment held at 4.1%.

The combination of resilient employment and persistent producer inflation reduces the urgency for the Fed to support the economy with lower borrowing costs. For the US Dollar Index, that combination has provided renewed support after periods of weakness earlier this year.

The remaining question is whether consumer inflation confirms the same trend.

US CPI Is the Next Major Test for the Dollar

Attention now shifts immediately to the US Consumer Price Index report on Friday. The Bureau of Labor Statistics is scheduled to release August CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET on September 11. The report could prove even more important for the September Fed decision because it provides a clearer picture of the inflation pressures directly affecting consumers.

A hotter-than-expected CPI reading could strengthen the case for a September rate hike and provide further support for the US dollar and Treasury yields. Conversely, softer underlying inflation could temper the recent hawkish repricing and limit the dollar’s advance. That makes Friday’s CPI release the next major catalyst for the US Dollar Index.

Oil Above $100 Complicates the Fed Inflation Outlook

The inflation story is also becoming increasingly tied to energy markets. Brent crude has climbed above $100 per barrel as the Middle East conflict raises concerns over global oil supplies. Reuters reported Brent around $105 on Thursday as geopolitical tensions intensified.

Higher oil prices can affect transportation, manufacturing and consumer costs, potentially keeping inflation elevated even if other components begin to cool.

That leaves the Fed facing a difficult combination of a resilient labour market and renewed commodity-driven inflation. For the dollar, continued pressure from energy prices could reinforce expectations that US monetary policy will remain restrictive for longer.

US Dollar Index Outlook: CPI Could Decide the Next Move

The US Dollar Index outlook has strengthened following the August PPI report, with higher Treasury yields and rising Fed rate-hike expectations providing support. However, Friday’s CPI report is likely to determine whether that move can extend.

Another upside inflation surprise would reinforce the argument for a September Fed hike and could keep the dollar supported. A softer core CPI reading would challenge that view and could trigger some unwinding of the latest move.

For now, the combination of hotter producer inflation, a resilient US labour market and elevated oil prices keeps the near-term US dollar outlook supported ahead of CPI.

Why is the US Dollar Index rising today?

The US Dollar Index is strengthening after August PPI inflation came in slightly hotter than expected, increasing expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates at its September meeting.

What does higher PPI mean for the US dollar?

Higher producer inflation can strengthen expectations for tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. Higher US interest rates and Treasury yields can, in turn, provide support for the dollar.

Will the Fed raise interest rates in September?

Markets are pricing approximately a 70% probability of a 25-basis-point rate increase following the latest PPI report, although Friday’s CPI data could materially change those expectations.
